title: Depleted inventories leave oil markets exposed to further supply disruptions
gist: World Bank October 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook oil summary: a Middle East conflict cut global oil supply by ~9 mb/d y/y in 2026Q2, drawing inventories ~2.4 mb/d from March-September to the bottom of their 2021-25 range, with OECD government stocks at 30+-year lows. Brent is forecast at $91/bbl for 2026, $79 in 2027 and $70 in 2028 as the market shifts to surplus in 2027Q2, but near-term risks are skewed up given depleted buffers (adverse case $105/bbl in 2027).

insights.claim: Front-month Brent crude futures climbed above $115/bbl in late October 2026 before easing to nearly $95/bbl in the first week of November as renewed active conflict in the Middle East appeared less likely.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Oil is trading on conflict headlines; volatility remains elevated.
insights.locator: Front-month Brent crude futures climbed

insights.claim: After Iran and the United States failed to reach a follow-on agreement to their June 2026 memorandum of understanding, Brent fluctuated between $75 and $100/bbl and then stayed above $100/bbl in September and October.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: US-Iran diplomacy is the key swing factor for crude prices.
insights.locator: Front-month Brent crude futures climbed

insights.claim: The European diesel premium over Brent averaged about $91/bbl in September 2026, a record high, and U.S. retail diesel prices averaged nearly $6.20 per gallon in October.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Middle distillate cracks are extreme; refiners with intact capacity earn windfall margins, diesel-heavy users face cost squeeze.
insights.quote: The European diesel premium over Brent averaged about $91/bbl in September, a record high
insights.locator: Front-month Brent crude futures climbed

insights.claim: Refinery damage in the Middle East delayed recovery of refined-product exports including diesel even as crude exports rebounded.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Product tightness can outlast crude normalization.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: By early October 2026 Middle Eastern oil exports were near 2025 levels, supported by ship-to-ship transfers, untracked shipments and pipelines bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Hormuz bypass infrastructure and shadow logistics proved crucial resilience channels.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: Global oil output fell about 9 mb/d (8.5%) year-on-year in 2026Q2 and 7 mb/d in Q3, largely in Saudi Arabia and Iraq, and gains from six major producers including Brazil, Kazakhstan and the United States offset just 18 percent of gross losses.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Non-Gulf supply response was weak; spare-capacity narrative was oversold.
insights.quote: Gains in six major producers—including Brazil, Kazakhstan, and the United States—offset just 18 percent of gross losses.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: Global oil supply is projected to fall 5.5 mb/d (5.2%) in 2026, the steepest annual decline in over four decades apart from 2020.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Historic supply shock frames 2026 as a structural energy-security event.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: Global oil demand is projected to shrink 2.6 mb/d (2.5%) in 2026, a decline surpassed only in 1980 and 2020, with consumption falls concentrated in EMDEs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Demand destruction in emerging markets signals growth damage from the price shock.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: China contributed about 35 percent of the decline in EMDE oil consumption, partly because electric vehicles displaced oil.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: EV penetration in China is now visibly reducing oil demand; the shock may accelerate permanent substitution.
insights.quote: China contributed about 35 percent of the decline in EMDE oil consumption, partly as electric vehicles displaced oil.
insights.locator: Middle Eastern crude exports have rebounded

insights.claim: The implied oil market deficit widened to 2.9 mb/d in 2026Q2, and observed global inventories fell about 2.4 mb/d on average from March to September, moving from near the top to near the bottom of their 2021-25 range.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Thin buffers raise price convexity to any new disruption.
insights.locator: Lower inventories have left oil markets

insights.claim: Although global stocks totaled about 7.8 billion barrels, much was in transit, needed for operations or otherwise not readily available, so effective buffers are thinner than headline figures.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Headline inventory numbers overstate usable cushion.
insights.locator: Lower inventories have left oil markets

insights.claim: OECD government oil stocks reached their lowest level in over three decades and U.S. strategic reserves remained at their lowest since 1982.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Limited policy firepower for a second shock; SPR refill demand later is a price support.
insights.quote: U.S. strategic reserves remained at their lowest since 1982
insights.locator: Lower inventories have left oil markets

insights.claim: In early October 2026 International Energy Agency members agreed to accelerate release of 100 million barrels of emergency stocks through January 2027, initially prioritizing diesel.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Further drains strategic buffers; diesel focus confirms product tightness.
insights.locator: Lower inventories have left oil markets

insights.claim: The World Bank forecasts Brent to average nearly $100/bbl in 2026Q4 and $91/bbl for 2026, falling to $79/bbl in 2027 and $70/bbl in 2028.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Consensus-style path implies a steep backwardated decline; positioning for normalization is the base case.
insights.locator: Oil prices are projected to ease

insights.claim: The baseline assumes sustained recovery in Middle Eastern crude shipments, Gulf refinery throughput back to pre-conflict levels by 2027Q2, and a rebound in Russian crude output.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Watch Gulf refinery restarts and Russian output as forecast tripwires.
insights.locator: Oil prices are projected to ease

insights.claim: Oil consumption is expected to recover in 2027 but remain about 0.5 mb/d below 2025 levels, while supply returns to about 106 mb/d, near its 2025 level.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Some demand loss looks permanent, a bearish structural signal.
insights.locator: Oil prices are projected to ease

insights.claim: The oil market is projected to enter surplus in 2027Q2, allowing inventories to recover about 80 percent of their 2026 drawdown by end-2027.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Surplus timing is a key catalyst for bearish crude positioning.
insights.locator: Oil prices are projected to ease

insights.claim: With inventories depleted, even modest additional supply losses could trigger sharp oil price increases, leaving near-term risks tilted to the upside.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Asymmetric upside risk argues for hedging crude/diesel exposure near term.
insights.quote: With inventories already depleted, even modest additional supply losses could trigger sharp price increases.
insights.locator: Near-term risks to oil prices remain

insights.claim: Renewed hostilities could reverse the recovery in Strait of Hormuz shipments, and attacks on Gulf pipelines, Red Sea shipping or Russian oil infrastructure could worsen crude and product shortages.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Key geopolitical flashpoints to monitor for oil spikes.
insights.locator: Near-term risks to oil prices remain

insights.claim: In an adverse scenario where Gulf production falls about 5 mb/d in 1H 2027 and Russian exports stay constrained, Brent would average $105/bbl in 2027, about 33 percent above baseline.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Quantified tail scenario for stress testing.
insights.locator: Near-term risks to oil prices remain

insights.claim: A more restrictive OPEC+ production policy is an additional upside price risk, while downside risks later include durable conflict resolution, stronger non-OPEC+ supply growth and faster EV adoption.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Risk balance shifts from upside near-term to downside over the forecast horizon.
insights.locator: Near-term risks to oil prices remain
